purpose: Runtime policy for Milestone 9 (Failure Pattern Registry and Governed Improvement Proposals, src/tools/aggregate-diagnostics.ts). Organizational memory over diagnostics the validator already emits -- an aggregator, not a new engine.

boundary.network_transmission: never, by default or implicitly. Any future external or cross-organization aggregation requires a separate milestone and Human Owner decision.
boundary.note: See DEC-013, DEC-015. This boundary is not a default that can be silently widened -- widening it is the separate decision this file describes, not a configuration change to this file.

storage.note: One immutable file per validation run, written once and never reopened -- two runs cannot collide by construction, because two runs never share a file. FAILURE-PATTERNS.json is rebuildable from these events at any time and is never itself the source of truth; a corrupted registry is a rebuild, not a data-loss event.

field_disposition._note: 'Metadata-only' is not a privacy guarantee by itself -- a bare artifact path can disclose a subject without a byte of content (customers/acme/fraud-investigation.md). Every field carries an explicit, auditable disposition rather than a blanket policy. Independent AI Reviewer's independent review of the first implementation found item_id normalization only replaced digits (an alphabetic id such as 'ACME-fraud-case' passed through unchanged) and execution_path was copied verbatim from PROJECT.md without enum validation despite being declared retain-as-closed-enum here -- both are now allowlist/enum-validated, never pattern-substituted or copied raw.

clustering.note: Never a raw occurrence count -- twenty reruns against one unfixed defect must register as one problem, not twenty. A cluster is scored on how many DISTINCT dimensions it spans.

candidate_threshold.note: All three must be met. A cluster confined to one project or one unresolved item, however many times it re-fired, does not cross this threshold.

improvement_candidate.note: A candidate must weigh the full remedy set -- 'add a new rule' is never the default, matching this roadmap's existing prohibition on rules added only to increase perceived coverage. A candidate whose disposition_summary is dominated by false_positive should propose fixing the rule, not adding another one.
improvement_candidate.status_change_requires: a DEC-### for any status other than proposed when the candidate was AI-authored

rule_lifecycle.invariant: A rule with lifecycle=experimental may carry severity info or warn only -- never fail, fail_release, or any blocking severity. Promotion experimental -> enforced requires a DEC-### and a ROADMAP.md entry.
